formats.key: swap((address token0, address token1, bytes32 config) poolKey, bool isToken1, int128 amount, uint96 sqrtRatioLimit, uint256 skipAhead, int256 calculatedAmountThreshold)
effects: Exact input (amount > 0): the signer pays exactly `amount` of the pool token chosen by isToken1. Router.handleLockData uses payFrom(swapper, ...) for an ERC-20, or forwards router ETH when token0 is address(0).
Exact input: the signer (msg.sender) receives the other pool token, at least calculatedAmountThreshold, or the call reverts.
Exact output (amount < 0): the signer receives exactly |amount| of the chosen token and pays the other token, at most -calculatedAmountThreshold.

Native ETH (token0 == address(0)) is paid from the router's ETH balance, so the signer has to attach msg.value. Any msg.value above what is used stays in the router, and anyone can take it with refundNativeToken().
The ERC-20 input is pulled with transferFrom, which uses the signer's allowance to the router.
formats.shown: "Swap 1000000" with the two pool token addresses, a Token 0/Token 1 enum, and the amount and threshold as raw signed integers. Price limit, skip ahead and config are optional. No native value is shown.

findings.title: swap (isToken1, threshold) is payable, but the screen never shows the ETH sent (@.value).
findings.evidence: Router.sol swap(...) is `external payable`. In handleLockData, native token0 swaps spend router ETH (`_swap(value, ...)`, `safeTransferETH(address(ACCOUNTANT), ...)`). Unused ETH stays in the router, and PayableMulticallable.refundNativeToken lets any caller take it. The descriptor has no `@.value` field.
findings.fix: Add a field {"path":"@.value","label":"ETH sent","format":"amount"}.

findings.title: swap (isToken1) shows the specified amount as a raw signed integer, with no token and no in/out meaning.
findings.evidence: descriptor: amount format "raw", label "Specified amount". Interpolated intent "Swap {amount}" renders as "Swap 1000000" (case 0). Router devdoc: "positive for exact input, negative for exact output".
findings.fix: Relabel it, e.g. "Amount (positive = you pay this, negative = you receive this)", and say in the intent that the token is the one picked by 'Specified pool token'. A single tokenPath cannot pick token0 or token1 from isToken1.

findings.title: swap (isToken1): the minimum received / maximum paid is shown as a raw 'Amount threshold' with no token.
findings.evidence: Router.handleLockData: `if (amountCalculated < calculatedAmountThreshold) revert SlippageCheckFailed`. The calculated amount is in the other pool token. descriptor: calculatedAmountThreshold format "raw", label "Amount threshold". Case 0 shows "1".
findings.fix: Relabel it, e.g. "Minimum received of the other pool token (negative = maximum paid), base units".

findings.title: swap (isToken1): native ETH pool token 0 (address(0)) shows as a zero address, not as ETH.
findings.evidence: constants.sol: `NATIVE_TOKEN_ADDRESS = address(0)`. descriptor: poolKey.token0 is addressName with types ["token"] and no native mapping.
findings.fix: Add a note or label saying that 0x000…000 means native ETH. For tokenAmount fields, use nativeCurrencyAddress.

findings.title: swap (isToken1): the intent "Swap {amount}" names neither the token paid nor the token received.
findings.evidence: interpolatedIntent "Swap {amount}" renders as "Swap 1000000" in case 0, where the swap is USDC to WETH.
findings.fix: Use an intent that names the pool tokens, e.g. "Swap {amount} in {poolKey.token0}/{poolKey.token1} pool".

findings.title: swap (isToken1): a price limit of 0 means 'no limit', but it is shown as a raw '0'.
findings.evidence: swapParameters.sol withDefaultSqrtRatioLimit replaces 0 with MIN/MAX_SQRT_RATIO. descriptor: sqrtRatioLimit is raw and optional. Case 0 shows "0".
findings.fix: Label it "Price limit (sqrt ratio, 0 = none)".

formats.key: swap((address token0, address token1, bytes32 config) poolKey, bool isToken1, int128 amount, uint96 sqrtRatioLimit, uint256 skipAhead, int256 calculatedAmountThreshold, address recipient)
effects: Exact input: the signer pays exactly `amount` of the token chosen by isToken1, as an ERC-20 transferFrom or as router ETH when token0 is address(0).
The other pool token goes to `recipient`, not to the signer: at least the threshold for exact input, exactly |amount| for exact output.
